completedTasks.title: Check how task tracking is hooked into Hermes: do we emit all the data, is emitting even possible
completedTasks.summary: Evidence-first research (docs/work/2026-08-02-hermes-task-tracking.md, 14 findings: 10 measured, 4 read). Answers: (1) NOT hooked — the four task hooks (session-start-tracking, task-checkpoint, task-checkpoint-session-end, dispatch-gate) are Claude-only by design; validate.py's exemptions claim Hermes produces no transcript JSONL to parse; the Hermes plugin registers only on_session_start/pre_llm_call/post_tool_call (drift, context, observer). (2) NO data emitted — every tracked task's checkpoints are all-zero (contextTokens 0, byModel {}, cumulative zeros); transcriptPath null everywhere; two of three recorded session ids do not exist in ~/.hermes/state.db (not pruned: auto_prune False, 0 archived rows; not Claude sessions either — no ~/.claude/projects entry for ai-raccon); subagent tokens recorded only via manual task_tracker.py subagent (token count not exposed by delegate_task's live return). (3) EMITTING IS POSSIBLE — Hermes state.db stores per-session + per-model tokens (sessions, session_model_usage), async_delegations maps delegations to child sessions with full token counts and its result_json carries {input, output} tokens per delegation, hook payloads carry session_id (incl. post_api_request per-call usage), and hermes insights / --usage-file / sessions export already aggregate the numbers. The exemptions' premise (no usable session data in Hermes) is false. Two adversarial passes: claims verifier 12/12 confirmed; code-reviewer gate on the record F1-F13 ACCURATE with 4 surgical fixes applied (F5 subagent entries, F6 current-session.json writers, F12 reconciliation wording, request-dump claim in Still open — all 17 dumps are error captures). Full suite 3073 passed, 18 skipped; index build check clean. Docs-only (research record + docs/work README row); no shipped-surface change, no VERSION bump.

completedTasks.title: Research: Gherkin + SpecBinder as a create-task-spec elicitation layer
completedTasks.summary: Validated the create-task-spec proposal. Two premises corrected: .specb is NOT a second document format (SpecBinder's supportedFileExtensions defaults to {feature,specb} - two aliases, identical Gherkin; emitting both makes convention-based discovery generate duplicate test classes), and the task-with-spec wrapper skill is unnecessary (differential-feature-refactor already chains owner-gate-review inline). Owner clarified the skill must EXTRACT knowledge by questioning, not propose content - which makes SpecBinder's own Claude commands (proposal-first, 'suggest 2-6 plausible rules') the anti-pattern, and dotnet-claude-kit's /spec (MIT, question-first) the pole to borrow from. Key insight: Gherkin's grammar is a question generator with an objective stop condition - a rule with no scenario and a scenario with no steps are greppable holes forming the open-question queue; SpecBinder tags step-less scenarios @new natively, so a half-elicited spec compiles to a failing suite (TDD RED as a build artifact). Blocking risk: no jvm stack here and SpecBinder is GPL-3.0 vs this repo's MIT, so it cannot be dogfooded - recommended stack-neutral skill proven against pytest-bdd/cucumber-js, SpecBinder behind a gated extension. No code changed; research only.

completedTasks.title: Trim docs/ to product documentation; move plans/reviews/designs/specs to .tmp (0.39.1)
completedTasks.summary: docs/ had become two trees sharing a directory - one documenting ai-badger, one documenting the building of it. 32 of the 51 non-changelog documents were the second kind (plans, session checkpoints, waves, reviews, audits, incident post-mortems, research passes, superseded designs and specs); those 32 plus the 3 files under .hermes/plans/ moved to a newly gitignored .tmp/, leaving 19: 11 ADRs and their index, plus 7 references. Selection test was 'would a reader of the product documentation lose something true', and every candidate was re-verified against the code at 0.39.0 before being carried forward - anything unverifiable was dropped rather than copied. Knowledge folded forward: framework-architecture.md gained scaffold.py's real shape (one Scaffolder holding a ScaffoldContext plus six collaborators) and the fact that proxy files were dropped, not deferred; hermes-claude-compatibility.md gained the learned-skill sync contract (the largest loss the move would otherwise have caused - a shipped feature that writes into a consumer's repo, described nowhere reachable); authoring-a-feature.md gained the mcp-servers.json contract it had only forward-referenced; scripts.md gained call-behaviorist. Reading thirty documents against the code caught two statements that had stopped being true: RELEASING.md claimed the untagged-release check was informational (0.35.3 made it return 1) and SECURITY.md miscounted unsafe_literals.py fixture matches at three (one remains). 22 docstrings and comments across features/, skills/ and tests/ stopped citing documents that no longer open. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the ADR and changelog links to the moved files were not repaired - an ADR is append-only under ADR-0001 and editing a past changelog falsifies what that release said, so repairing them would mean falsifying a record to satisfy a link checker; 9 prefixes went into .docs-guard-ignore instead, which is what that file is for. COMPLICATION: partway through, another session merged two unrelated streams into task/clean-up-docs - the #110 drift fix (drift compares the framework, not the project against itself) and an 'every check must prove it can fail' testing stream adding tests/test_every_check_can_fail.py - and cut release 0.40.0 on the branch, so PR #111 squash-merged 0.39.1 and 0.40.0 together as 147f98e, wider than its title. Audited 2026-07-29 before closing the record: the squash tree is byte-identical to the branch tip, all 35 deletions and 3 additions survive on main at 0.45.0, and the gates pass (docs_guard 109 documents, index.json up to date, 1624 tests passing).

completedTasks.title: Commit-reminder hook: advisory PostToolUse nudge for all three agents (0.35.0-0.35.2)
completedTasks.summary: Built a common/ hook that watches live `git status --porcelain` uncommitted-file count after edit-shaped tool calls and nudges (never blocks/denies/gates - additionalContext only, honoring the 0.33.0 no-third-party-tool-call-interception precedent) once a threshold (default 5, AI_BADGER_COMMIT_REMINDER_THRESHOLD) crosses, with a ratchet-debounce that re-arms after every commit instead of latching forever (avoids the 'adjustments reported as drifted forever' bug class). Impact reason is pluggable: a pure file-count default (features/common/skills/commit-reminder/scripts/impact_estimator.py), extended by an opt-in (AI_BADGER_COMMIT_REMINDER_IMPACT=graph) code-review-graph CLI subprocess call for real blast-radius data, guarded so any failure/absence falls back silently and the ~15-20s call only runs once the cheap check already decided to fire. Shipped for all three agents from one shared commit_reminder.py/impact_estimator.py core: Claude+Copilot via the existing hooks-manifest.json/hooks.json PostToolUse wiring (fixed Copilot's adjust_hooks.py to also carry the matcher field through, previously dropped), Hermes via post_tool_observer stashing a pending reminder that pre_llm_inject_context surfaces on the next turn. Mid-task user feedback (f: marker) required instrumenting with the existing debug_log/call-behaviorist audit facility rather than shipping silently, under component name commit_reminder_hook; a follow-on continuation (0.35.1) generalized that same vendored-debug_log pattern to the 5 other framework hooks that had never called it. PR #105; 1366 tests passing at 0.35.2.

completedTasks.title: Full-project multi-agent code review + Wave 1 remediation (0.19.0)
completedTasks.summary: Ran 8 parallel reviewers (architecture, security, python, ai-agent design, skill engineering, tests, silent failures, docs) over the whole project, then an Opus integrating pass that VERIFIED every Critical against the code rather than trusting it: 23 raw -> 19 distinct -> 7 confirmed, 12 downgraded to Important, 5 sub-claims rejected (incl. security's 'live RCE', correctly latent, and docs' 'nothing shipped since v0.2.0', disproved by plugin.json). Root cause behind four dead features: tests validate synthetic fixtures instead of the real catalog, so install_skills emitting zero install commands and mcp_index_hook targeting a nonexistent script both shipped green. Wave 1 fixed the five destructive Criticals TDD-first: sync_plugin_skills --dry-run rmtree'd before its own guard (wiped all 8 shipped skill dirs); five sites treated an unparseable config as {} then overwrote it, two of them machine-global (~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.hermes/config.yaml); a user-scope Hermes hook exec'd a cwd-derived path the framework never creates (removed, NOT renamed - renaming to the real mcp_index.py would have armed it; guard test parametrized over both names); install_cron could replace the whole crontab when crontab -l failed, and ran by default (now opt-in --cron); the learned-skill secret scanner skipped symlinks while copytree dereferenced them, leaking outside-root file contents into an un-gitignored dir. Also aligned pre-commit's pylint with pyproject on E0401 - the two gates disagreed, arbitrarily failing any small new test file. 691 -> 727 tests. Waves 2-5 planned but deliberately unshipped; hard constraint recorded: the auto-wm denylist (F-12) MUST land before session_start_hook is wired (F-07), or the framework ships a machine that can enable unattended auto-approval of its own tool calls. PR #78.

completedTasks.title: Hermes learned-skills sync (#67) + reverse #58 + plugin-hook cwd fix (#76)
completedTasks.summary: Reviewed docs/research/hermes-learned-skills-sync.md and corrected four load-bearing claims: external_dirs was already tried and reverted (#58/v0.7.1); the ~/.hermes/skills/ symlinks still exist on disk so a naive scan re-imports framework skills; NOTHING distributed .ai-badger/skills/ to any agent; and the hook mechanism is the Python plugin this repo already ships, not ~/.hermes/hooks/. Wrote a staged TDD plan with acceptance criteria, then implemented it: learned_skills_sync.py (5 gates, learned.json provenance, opt-in --reconcile, unsafe-literal refusal), feed-badger per-skill grouping, post_tool_call wiring + ~/.hermes/plugins install, and the #58 reversal restoring namespaced symlinks without the original rmtree data-loss hazard. Key discovery beyond scope: Hermes passes NO cwd to any plugin hook, and names the prompt kwarg user_message not message — so the drift notice, the pre_llm drift line, and the MCP index logging had never fired (#76, fixed). CodeQL's clear-text-logging alert was name-heuristic, not flow-based: Copilot autofix traded alert 13 for 14 and cost CLI output, so it was reverted and the identifiers renamed to unsafe-literal terms, which cleared it. PRs #73/#74/#75 + recovery #77; 683 tests green at 0.18.0.
